mission: Test the historical topographic hypothesis for the Biggeh Abaton against the 2024-2026 CNRS-SCA archaeological survey without converting textual sacred geography into a biological-relic claim.

source_chain: Hermann Junker reconstruction of the Abaton topography
Charly De Mare, Ci-git Osiris, l'Abaton de Biggeh, 2016

proposed_locus.description: extreme southern end of the indentation on the eastern coast of Biggeh, where the southernmost modern village houses stood in the satellite image used by De Mare
proposed_locus.interpretive_basis: Junker argued that the flat zone between the northern and southern peaks did not fit the sacred-mound/high-mountain terminology, while the extreme southern tip lacked sufficient room; he therefore placed the tomb and grove at the southern end of the eastern coastal indentation.

institutions: collaborating Italian institutions reported by Louvre 2026
2024_public_facts: mission topographer Damien Laisney was producing a modern map of Biggeh
the island was systematically divided into distinct archaeological zones
the surviving temple is substantially inundated and its quay is completely underwater
the staircase into the temple is regularly flooded
lateral chambers and architectural blocks are partly underwater
the temple interior is obscured by Nile silt and dense vegetation
the mission stated that a systematic excavation program would target the internal area between the pronaos and the rocky mountain
modern_mission.2026_public_status: Louvre described the joint mission as conducting preventive archaeology because the Biggeh temple is submerged for much of the year.

overlay_result.key_finding: The De Mare/Junker proposed Abaton locus is not the same point as the commonly mapped surviving Temple of Senmet/Bigeh. Using a secondary public temple coordinate near 24.022098,32.886371 only as an orientation anchor, the proposed locus lies roughly 211 m to the south-southwest. This distance is a GIS orientation result, not a survey-grade archaeological measurement.
overlay_result.critical_distinction: The mission's publicly announced excavation between the pronaos and rocky mountain appears to concern the immediate surviving-temple interior. Public information reviewed so far does not establish that the separate De Mare/Junker locus approximately 200 m south-southwest has already been excavated or tested.
overlay_result.strongest_next_test: Obtain the mission's georeferenced 2024-2026 zonation/site plan and determine whether 24.020283,32.885758 lies inside a numbered survey/excavation zone, then check for mapped walls, terraces, cavities, wells, palaeochannels, mound deposits, sealed ritual deposits or negative archaeological results at that point.

outreach.recipient_route: Carole Eveno, Mondes pharaoniques UMR 8167, cc UMR 8167 laboratory, with request to forward to Gihane Zaki / Biggeh mission
request: whether 24.020283,32.885758 falls within the current concession and a numbered archaeological zone
whether the southern end of the eastern indentation has been mapped or tested
a shareable georeferenced 2024-2026 site plan or published reference
known buried architecture, cavities, wells, palaeochannels, sealed deposits or ritual material near the locus
whether new survey data supports or contradicts the older Junker/De Mare reconstruction

canonical_formula: OLD_TEXT_AND_MAP -> GEOREFERENCED_HYPOTHESIS -> MODERN_ZONE_MAP -> NONINVASIVE_SURVEY -> EXCAVATION_CONTEXT -> CONTENT -> ONLY_THEN_IDENTITY
canonical_seal: WE HAVE A TESTABLE PLACE, NOT A FOUND BODY PART.
